facts.statement: Ford's current board has 14 directors, all incumbent nominees for the May 11, 2023 election.
Kimberly A. Casiano is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2003.
Alexandra Ford English, an incumbent nominee, was first elected at the 2021 Annual Meeting and remains a director after her June 17, 2022 employment departure.
James D. Farley, Jr. is an incumbent nominee and director since 2020.
Henry Ford III, an incumbent nominee, was first elected at the 2021 Annual Meeting.
William Clay Ford, Jr. is an incumbent nominee and director since 1988.
William W. Helman IV is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2011.
Jon M. Huntsman, Jr. is an incumbent nominee and director since 2020, with earlier board service in 2012-2017.
William E. Kennard is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2015.
John C. May is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2021.
Beth E. Mooney is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2019.
Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2017.
John L. Thornton is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 1996.
John B. Veihmeyer is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2017.
John S. Weinberg is an incumbent nominee and independent director since 2016.
Anthony F. Earley, Jr. served as a director through the 2022 Annual Meeting and did not stand for re-election.
Edsel B. Ford II is explicitly identified as a former Ford director.
Earley retired following the May 2022 shareholder meeting; the Committee recommended reducing board size from 15 to 14 at that transition.

The Board determined nine nominees independent with no material relationship: Casiano, Helman, Kennard, May, Mooney, Vojvodich Radakovich, Thornton, Veihmeyer and Weinberg; they represent 64% of nominees.
The Board determined Earley independent during his service, including under the stated heightened SEC independence standards for compensation committees.
facts.stated_time: During Earley's service before the 2022 Annual Meeting

facts.statement: William Clay Ford, Jr. is not independent under Ford's Corporate Governance Principles.
William Clay Ford, Jr. has chaired the Board since January 1999 and been Executive Chair since September 2006; the Chair and CEO roles are separate.
John L. Thornton is the appointed Lead Independent Director, serving in that role since 2022.
A reprinted shareholder proposal identifies Anthony Earley as Lead Director in its historical voting discussion.
facts.stated_time: Shareholder proposal discussing 2021 voting; exact leadership dates unstated

facts.statement: Five standing committees exist: Audit; Compensation, Talent and Culture; Finance; Nominating and Governance; Sustainability, Innovation and Policy.
Audit has three members: John B. Veihmeyer (Chair), Kimberly A. Casiano and Beth E. Mooney.
Compensation, Talent and Culture has four members: Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich (Chair), John C. May, John L. Thornton and John S. Weinberg.
Finance members are William Clay Ford, Jr. (Chair), Alexandra Ford English, Henry Ford III, Helman, Kennard, May, Thornton and Weinberg.
Nominating and Governance members are Kennard (Chair), Casiano, Helman, May, Mooney, Vojvodich Radakovich, Thornton, Veihmeyer and Weinberg.
Sustainability, Innovation and Policy members are Helman (Chair), Casiano, Alexandra Ford English, Henry Ford III, William Clay Ford, Jr., Huntsman, Kennard, Vojvodich Radakovich and Weinberg.
William Clay Ford, Jr. has chaired Finance since 2007 and previously chaired it from 1995 until October 2001.
Earley was a Compensation, Talent and Culture member during 2022 until May 12, 2022.
The reprinted shareholder proposal identifies Anthony Earley as chair of the 'management pay committee'.
facts.stated_time: Shareholder proposal discussing 2021 voting; exact chair tenure unstated

facts.statement: Audit is fully independent; the Board additionally determined Casiano, Mooney, Vojvodich Radakovich and Veihmeyer satisfy heightened SEC audit independence standards.
All four current Compensation, Talent and Culture members are independent, including under additional NYSE compensation committee standards.
Nominating and Governance is composed entirely of independent directors under NYSE, SEC and Ford standards.
The filing determines each current Audit member meets NYSE financial literacy requirements.
The Board designated Audit Chair John B. Veihmeyer an Audit Committee financial expert under SEC regulations and applicable NYSE rules.
None of the five 2022 Compensation members was an employee or current/former Ford officer during committee service, or had a disclosable relationship.
Ford's assessment credits Casiano with marketing, international, finance, risk and sustainability expertise; nomination reasons emphasize global leadership and customer engagement.
Ford credits English with marketing, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons cite brand management, strategy, autonomous vehicles and family stewardship.
Ford credits Farley with manufacturing, CEO, marketing, international, finance, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons cite Ford+ digital and electric leadership.
Ford credits Henry Ford III with marketing, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons cite cross-functional operations, investor relations and family stewardship.

Ford credits William Clay Ford, Jr. with manufacturing, CEO, international, finance, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize stakeholder relationships and mobility leadership.
Ford credits Helman with finance, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize technology investment, social media marketing and innovation.
Ford credits Huntsman with CEO, international, government, finance, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize global and environmental policy experience.
Ford credits Kennard with international, government, finance, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons cite policy, law, telecommunications and private equity.
Ford credits May with manufacturing, CEO, international, finance, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons cite connectivity, global operations and information technology.
Ford credits Mooney with CEO, government, finance, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize banking and executive expertise.
Ford credits Vojvodich Radakovich with manufacturing, marketing, finance, technology, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize software innovation and growth-company advice.
Ford credits Thornton with CEO, international, finance, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize finance and emerging markets, especially China.
Ford credits Veihmeyer with CEO, international, finance, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize accounting, regulatory environments and executive leadership.
Ford credits Weinberg with CEO, international, finance, risk and sustainability; nomination reasons emphasize banking, capital markets and Ford-specific financial advice.
The nominee matrix identifies four women: Casiano, English, Mooney and Vojvodich Radakovich; Kennard is Black/African American, Casiano Hispanic, and the other twelve White.

unresolved.reason: The filing describes a 15-to-14 reduction following the May 2022 meeting but separately calls 14 directors then-current at last year's meeting; historical count/timing is not reconciled.
Earley's Lead Director and 'management pay committee' chair labels come from an unendorsed reprinted shareholder proposal; exact tenure and the informal committee's formal identity are unstated.
Vojvodich Radakovich's audit independence determination does not establish Audit membership; the current three-member Audit roster excludes her, and no membership dates are supplied.
